nodes.title: Count drag enters and leaves
nodes.why: Moving onto the text inside the zone fires dragenter on that text before dragleave on the zone, so switching off on every dragleave turns the highlight off while the pointer is still over the zone. Counting enters and leaves keeps the zone active until the drag has left all of it. A drop on the zone's text ends the drag with the count at 2 and no dragleave to bring it down, so every drop of files resets the count.
nodes.alternative: Ignore a dragleave whose relatedTarget is still inside the zone.
nodes.tradeoff: The relatedTarget test needs no counter, but it depends on the browser filling relatedTarget for drag events, which has not always been reliable. The counter depends on every dragenter having its dragleave; if one is lost, the zone stays lit until the next drop of files.

nodes.title: Only react to drags that carry files
nodes.why: Text or a link dragged from the page fires the same events. Until the drop, browsers keep dataTransfer.files empty, so only dataTransfer.types can tell that files are coming; checking it for Files keeps the zone dark for other drags, and stops a drop of text from clearing the rejection list.
nodes.alternative: Light the zone for any drag and filter the dropped items.
nodes.tradeoff: Simpler, but the zone then invites drops it will refuse, and the highlight no longer tells the user what will happen.

nodes.title: Cancel dragover on the zone and show the copy cursor

anchor.snippet: // Without this, the browser does not allow a drop here.

nodes.why: A browser allows a drop only where dragover was cancelled. The zone cancels it itself and sets dropEffect to copy, while the page-wide guard sets none everywhere else, so the cursor tells the user where a drop counts.
nodes.alternative: Leave dropEffect at the browser's default.
nodes.tradeoff: For files from the desktop the default is usually copy already, so setting it states the intent. A drag source that allowed only move or link would be refused by a copy effect, which desktop file drags never are.

nodes.title: Cancel file drags on the whole page
nodes.why: A receipt dropped a few pixels outside the zone would otherwise replace the page and lose every running upload. Cancelling dragover for files on window with dropEffect none tells the browser that a drop there does nothing, so it neither opens the file nor fires drop; cancelling drop too covers a drop that arrives anyway. Text drags pass through, so text fields still take them.
nodes.alternative: Make the whole page the drop zone.
nodes.tradeoff: A page-wide drop target is forgiving, but it gives no clear place to aim, and it takes drops that other widgets on the page may want.

nodes.title: Check the type, then the size
nodes.why: The browser gives each File a type and a size, so the check needs no reading of the file. The type comes first, so a large PDF is reported as the wrong type, the reason that matters to the user.
nodes.alternative: Check the size first, or check the file name's extension.
nodes.tradeoff: Size first tells the user to shrink a file they cannot upload anyway. An extension check reads the name instead of the type the browser reports, which it usually derives from that same extension; neither proves the content, so the server checks the bytes again. These checks go by the reported type.

nodes.title: Give every row its own key
nodes.why: Two receipts can share a name, such as two scans called receipt.png. A counter gives each row its own key, so its controller, its preview URL and its React key never collide with another row of the same name.
nodes.tradeoff: Names read well in the code, but the second file then replaces the first in every map, and removing one row stops or removes the other.

nodes.title: One AbortController per upload
nodes.why: Cancel, Remove and the unmount cleanup each need to stop one upload, or all of them. Keeping a controller per row in a ref lets every path abort the right one, and the fake upload, like fetch, stops its work when the signal aborts.
nodes.alternative: Keep a cancelled flag and ignore progress after it.
nodes.tradeoff: A flag hides the progress but leaves the upload and its timers running, which in a real app keeps sending bytes.

nodes.title: Treat an aborted upload as stopped, not failed
nodes.why: Aborting rejects the upload's promise too. Checking the signal keeps a cancelled row at Cancelled instead of turning it into Upload failed.
nodes.alternative: Check the error's name for AbortError.
nodes.tradeoff: The name check works for fetch and for this fake, but the signal is the source of truth and needs no knowledge of how each API names its error.

nodes.title: Hand focus to the button that replaces the clicked one
nodes.why: Cancel is replaced by Retry, Retry by Cancel, and Remove takes its whole row away; an upload that ends on its own takes Cancel away too. Without a hand-off, focus falls to the body: a screen reader loses its place, and browsers differ in where the next Tab goes. Each of these records where focus should go, and an effect moves it after the render.
nodes.alternative: Keep every button in the row and disable the ones that do not apply.
nodes.tradeoff: No element disappears, but browsers differ on whether a focused button keeps focus once it is disabled, and every row then carries buttons that cannot be used.

nodes.title: Create the preview URL once, when the file arrives
nodes.why: Each call to URL.createObjectURL makes a new URL that keeps its File alive until it is revoked. Making it in render makes one per render, and every progress report renders the row again; making it in the handler gives one URL for the life of the row.
nodes.alternative: Make the URL in an effect inside a row component and revoke it in that effect's cleanup.
nodes.tradeoff: The effect ties the URL to the row's lifetime without a ref, at the cost of a render per row with no image before the effect stores the URL.

nodes.title: Revoke every URL and stop every upload on unmount
nodes.why: Object URLs, and the Files they point at, live until they are revoked or the document unloads, and a single-page app rarely unloads. The cleanup holds the Map objects captured at mount; it sees the rows that exist when App unmounts because the maps are changed in place, never replaced.
nodes.alternative: Revoke the URLs only when App unmounts.
nodes.tradeoff: One cleanup is simpler, but every removed row keeps its File alive until the user leaves the screen.

nodes.title: Clear the picker's value after reading it
nodes.why: A file input fires change only when its selection changes, so choosing the same receipt twice would do nothing the second time. Clearing the value after reading its files makes every choice count.
nodes.alternative: Leave the value as it is.
nodes.tradeoff: Less code, but a user who removes a receipt and picks the same file again sees nothing happen.
